title: Willis-Type Stochastic Homogenization for Elastodynamics with an Inertial Corrector in an Inhomogeneous Medium
content: In this paper, we propose a Willis-type stochastic homogenization method for the linear elastodynamic equation in an inhomogeneous medium with a stationary random microstructure. The approach introduces an inertial corrector, which is generally neglected in most dynamic homogenization methods, and accounts for the inertial anisotropy of the microstructure, the mass enhancement effect, and the elasticity–inertia coupling. The passage from an inhomogeneous to a homogeneous medium is achieved through an asymptotic expansion of the elastodynamic equation up to order ε2, where ε is the scale-separation parameter between the microstructure and the macrostructure. This makes it possible to determine successively the static and inertial correctors, from which the effective mechanical properties are obtained analytically. The numerical implementation combines the stochastic finite element method (SFEM), adaptive Monte Carlo simulation, and the Newmark scheme. Compared with results from the literature, the Willis-type stochastic homogenization method for elastodynamics with an inertial corrector proves reliable for predicting the static and dynamic effective properties of inhomogeneous materials with a stationary and ergodic random microstructure, including inertial anisotropy and mass enhancement, which reflects the tensorial nature of the effective density.
